low_power_modes_summary.ahb_idle: Manager drives HTRANS=IDLE; bus is idle. Clock gating of HCLK is implementation-defined.
low_power_modes_summary.apb_idle: PSELx=0, PENABLE=0; bus is idle. PCLK can be gated by the integrator when no peripheral activity is needed.
low_power_modes_summary.apb_low_power_intent: APB was explicitly designed as a low-cost, low-power peripheral bus optimized for minimal power consumption and reduced interface complexity (Section 1.1).

fields.notes: Power-domain partitioning, voltage-domain crossings, power-gate sequencing, isolation cells, retention registers are deferred to the SoC integration spec (UPF / CPF). Neither IHI 0033C nor IHI 0024C defines a power-intent layer. APB's two-cycle minimum and lack of pipelining are intentionally chosen to reduce dynamic power on the peripheral bus.

evidence.quote: The Advanced Peripheral Bus (APB) is part of the Advanced Microcontroller Bus Architecture (AMBA) protocol family. It defines a low-cost interface that is optimized for minimal power consumption and reduced interface complexity. The APB protocol is not pipelined, use it to connect to low-bandwidth peripherals that do not require the high performance of the AXI protocol.
It is recommended that the address and write signals are not changed immediately after a transfer, but remain stable until another access occurs. This reduces power consumption.
